slides.title: Twin or double?|Room names, decoded
slides.body: What the room names really mean.

slides.title: Single.
slides.body: Made for one guest. The bed can be a single or a small double.

slides.title: Double.
slides.body: One bed for two people. Check the bed size if you like space.

slides.title: Twin.
slides.body: Two separate beds. Handy for friends or colleagues sharing a room.

slides.title: Superior or deluxe.
slides.body: Each hotel sets its own categories. Compare the size and the photos, not the name.

slides.title: Junior suite.
slides.body: Usually one bigger room with a sitting area, not a separate living room.

slides.title: Room assigned at check-in.
slides.body: Sometimes called run of house. The hotel picks your room type when you arrive.

slides.title: Know what you're booking?
slides.body: Compare rooms on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
Twin, double, superior, junior suite. Room names can be confusing.

Twin means two beds, double means one bed for two. Superior and deluxe are each hotel's own labels, so compare the size and the photos. A junior suite is usually one bigger room with a sitting area.

slides.title: Check-in day|6 mistakes to avoid
slides.body: Small things that slow you down at the desk.

slides.title: Arriving hours before check-in.
slides.body: Your room may not be ready. Ask to leave your bags and go explore.

slides.title: No ID at hand.
slides.body: Many hotels ask to see a passport or ID card. Keep it in your hand luggage.

slides.title: Only a debit card.
slides.body: Some hotels hold a deposit and prefer a credit card. Check the hotel's policy first.

slides.title: Not warning about a late arrival.
slides.body: Landing after midnight? Message the hotel so they know you're still coming.

slides.title: Forgetting the city tax.
slides.body: In many cities it's paid at the hotel on arrival. Keep a little budget for it.

slides.title: A name that doesn't match.
slides.body: The name on the booking should match the guest's ID. Double-check before you confirm.

slides.title: Amalfi Coast|where to stay, by vibe
slides.body: 5 towns, 5 very different trips.

slides.title: Positano
slides.body: Pastel houses stacked down the cliff, a lively beach and lots of steps.

slides.title: Amalfi
slides.body: The cathedral, the main ferry pier and buses along the coast.

slides.title: Ravello
slides.body: High above the sea, with the gardens of Villa Rufolo and Villa Cimbrone.

slides.title: Praiano
slides.body: Between Positano and Amalfi, smaller and slower, facing west.

slides.title: Sorrento
slides.body: Just off the coast, with trains to Naples and Pompeii and ferries to Capri.

slides.title: Which one is yours?
slides.body: Compare Amalfi Coast hotels on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
The Amalfi Coast is not one place. Each town sets a different pace.

Views? Positano. Ferries and buses? Amalfi. Quiet gardens? Ravello. Slow sunsets? Praiano. An easy base with trains? Sorrento.
